summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Hanna Dewo/243)

data.turoyo: E qām qḥīr, qām azzé nafəq. Nṣəfle ṭize, azzeyo.
data.translation: Yes, he up and got angry, he up and went away. He shook off his butt, he went away.

rationale: Second I.1 Preterit example; new body-part object in departure context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Keze/30)

data.turoyo: Nṣəfla ruḥa mad+dawme, palle lə+ṭrela bruḥa.
data.translation: She shook the leaves off herself (lit. ‘she shook herself off the trees’); she did not leave a leaf upon herself.

rationale: Third I.1 Preterit example; personified tree extends inherited reflexive shaking. Retains edition literal note exposing the source-frame issue.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NI Three kinds of death/21)

data.turoyo: Hulele dabbūz, nṣəfle me ḥḏoḏe, lu+maloxo mtaḥte raġle šqile i+ruḥayḏe.
data.translation: He hit him with a mace, he shook him altogether, out from under his feet the angel took his soul.
data.ref: MAC NI Three kinds of death/21

rationale: Fourth I.1 Preterit example; external patient with me ḥḏoḏe, without interpreting it as dismemberment.

evidence.cite: MAC NI Three kinds of death/21

after: schütteln, abschütteln (auch um sauber zu kriegen);
rationale: The original purpose restriction excludes the externally caused violent shaking and departure gesture; the shared physical shaking meaning is retained.

summary: ruḥa expresses active reflexivity in the tree example; it is not Detransitive morphology. External-patient shaking in the death story broadens the argument frame while retaining the physical movement.

The nsf lookup confirms a distinct plucking example and an inherited note recommending relegation to nṣf. This does not establish identity of every sense; no automatic merger or etymology change is made.
The ṭize search finds no nṣf idiom. The lack of a listing does not establish that the departure gesture is conventional; no new idiom is published.
MAC NE Keze/30: why mad+dawme from the trees when the subject is the tree and the next clause identifies leaves? Verify noun and source preposition; no source correction is invented.
MAC NI Three kinds of death/21: is me ḥḏoḏe separative or intensive? The current broad shaking gloss deliberately leaves physical splitting unasserted.
MAC Hanna Dewo/243: is shaking ṭizo a conventional dismissive gesture or literal shaking clean? Confirm before making an Idiomatic phrases headword.
Editors: resolve the inherited nsf-to-nṣf suggestion while preserving the plucking evidence and uncertain etymology.
Personified tree subject retains the reflexive removal construction. A body-part shaking gesture occurs on angry departure; conventional contempt remains unconfirmed.
